variants.name: Explicit loop / iterator chain (stable default)
variants.implementation_notes: Stable Rust makes no tail-call promise: LLVM may turn a tail call into a jump at high optimization levels (sibling-call optimization), but nothing in the language or the reference guarantees it, and Drop glue, Result wrapping or a debug profile keep the frame. The stable realization is therefore the loop the pattern names - `loop`/`while let` with the accumulator in a mutable local - or the iterator chain (fold/try_fold/scan) that already encodes step-and-carry. Choose the loop when the iteration is a state machine, the iterator when it walks a sequence.
pitfalls: Release-only optimization: -C opt-level=3 may eliminate the frame, while a debug build or a small edit (wrapping the call in a match, using ?) keeps it - so a stack overflow can be profile-dependent.
Drop glue is work after the call: returning a value that owns a Drop type, or holding one across the recursive call, prevents the tail call even where the backend would otherwise form one.

Iterator adapters replace the loop but not arbitrary recursion: a helper that recurses while unwrapping Result per level still grows the stack and must be turned into an explicit loop with an error accumulator.

variants.name: Explicit tail calls with become (nightly)
variants.implementation_notes: Rust's explicit_tail_calls feature - unstable, tracking issue #112788 - adds the `become` expression, which requires the call in that position to be performed as a tail call. That is the only way to get a guarantee on stable-adjacent toolchains today, and because it is nightly-only it is suited to experiments and to code that already pins a nightly compiler, not to libraries. The rest of the pattern is unchanged: the accumulator travels in parameters and the base case returns directly.
pitfalls: The feature is unstable: it needs a nightly toolchain and can change, so a crate that depends on it cannot compile on stable.
`become` is not a drop-in for `return` in code with cleanup: the callee must be able to take over the frame, so owning locals with destructors force a restructure.
